data.narrative:
Amber Bio is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Basem Al-Shayeb and Jacob Borrajo that has raised $26M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public comparables in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression analysis proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($26M) as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next funding stage yields an implied valuation of $65M. Peer-median triangulation was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum threshold (0 of 3 required). Public-comp anchoring could not be applied because target revenue is not disclosed—a common limitation for private companies. The public sector median P/S multiple stands at 7.4x across the three biotech comparables, but without revenue data this multiple cannot be operationalized.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $55M to $75M, centered on $65M. This range reflects the median from stage-progression methodology with typical uncertainty bands applied. Key limitations include reliance on a single method and absence of revenue data that would enable cross-validation through public multiples. The true valuation will ultimately depend on technology differentiation and near-term financing momentum relative to stated private peers.
